analysis:
I reviewed three changes.

1) ClusterSetupWizardStore.swift head 99-115 adds ApprovalSetAside.setAt, a wall-clock time. A set-aside approval is taken again after ClusterApprovalFallback.failingSeconds. Older records with setAt nil are treated as already past that window. This changes local retry and availability behavior only. The coordinator still owns approval. The wall clock is operator-controlled (TB-003), but at worst that lets an operator re-take an approval the coordinator already issued. No change grants trust.

2) ClusterPublicModels.swift (new, head 1-131) hardcodes two declared public models with artifact SHA-256s, the pipeline and tensor_parallel families, and schedules 1 and 2. It also adds:
- requestEnvelope (head 90-94): media is allowed only when servesMedia is true; token limits are 1,048,576.
- families() (head 99-105): when artifactSHA256 is nil it returns the declared families, which is permissive.

3) DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift:
- Grants now carry records and an evidenceSHA256 over canonical JSON lines (head 185-205, 475-476).
- ownerServing gains declaredFamilies.
- publicTrafficLine merges declared families with record grants (head ~814-828), so it can say "qualified for public traffic" with no passing local record. It also adds a tensorAssistant not-offered line.

In the visible code these values feed display lines and owner-serving structs only. The line text itself says the coordinator's parity qualification decides each placement. No local admission gate visibly uses declaredFamilies.

Integration must check:
- ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts and release-fact generation. The comments at head 37-41 say release facts carry a grant and parity qualifications for the declared models, from which the coordinator derives approvals. If a declaration with no passing record is turned into coordinator-trusted parity evidence, that is a qualification-policy shift relevant to T-007, T-027, T-054 and A-017. Those consumers are not in this batch.
- Whether evidenceSHA256 binds to the evidenceDocument hash (head 46-47).
- Whether a nil artifact in families() reaches any gate rather than display only.
- Whether the tensorAssistant local-only rule is enforced outside display.

The threat model has no entry for distributed or cluster pair serving. A gap may need recording if public cluster serving is in scope. No concrete regression was found in the supplied code.
